headline: High-risk default interaction: Cursor can hand off workspace content to Kestra, creating dangerous prompt-injection, leakage, and action-cascade paths.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Cursor reads open files, clipboard contents, and workspace files, and can use MCP; Kestra can ingest files, stdin/stdout, and trigger downstream tasks. That creates a plausible path where attacker-controlled content in Cursor is forwarded into Kestra workflows or prompts. The pair is not blocked by isolation, so interaction risk is real.
conditions: IF Cursor copies untrusted file content into a Kestra task definition or parameter
IF Kestra parses Cursor-produced text as workflow instructions without validation
mitigations: Disable automatic handoff of generated text between tools
Add strict allowlists for fields accepted from Cursor
Require human review before Kestra executes Cursor-authored workflows
Use separate workspaces for editor and orchestrator
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging from Cursor to Kestra

B_data_leakage.rationale: Cursor touches source code, open files, and clipboard contents and has broad network egress to model providers; Kestra handles logs, inputs, variables, artifacts, database data, and cloud storage data. In default use, sensitive workspace data can flow from Cursor into Kestra outputs or external APIs, creating a realistic exfiltration path across the pair.
conditions: IF Cursor sends open-file content to a third-party model provider
IF Kestra receives secrets or PII in workflow inputs and writes them to logs, notifications, or artifacts
mitigations: Redact secrets before passing data from Cursor to Kestra
Turn off verbose logging in Kestra for sensitive workflows
Restrict Cursor to non-sensitive repositories
Use separate credentials for each agent
requires-engineering: enforce data-loss-prevention filters at the integration boundary

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents can write the filesystem and execute shells, and Cursor explicitly shares state via the local filesystem while Kestra writes to /app/storage and /tmp. Without locking or coordination primitives in either profile, concurrent edits or job outputs can overwrite each other, corrupt git state, or clobber workflow artifacts.
conditions: IF Cursor and Kestra target the same directory or repository
IF both agents modify git state or shared artifacts concurrently
mitigations: Assign disjoint directories to each agent
Pause Kestra jobs during Cursor edits to shared repos
Avoid concurrent git operations
Add file locks around shared outputs
requires-engineering: introduce orchestrator-level locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: Cursor can generate code, configs, and workflow text, and Kestra can execute declarative workflows, shell commands, and external actions such as email or cloud APIs. If Kestra treats Cursor output as authoritative, a mistaken or malicious instruction can cascade into real-world actions with little verification.
conditions: IF Kestra imports Cursor-generated workflow YAML without validation
IF Cursor-produced instructions are used to trigger Kestra tasks that send notifications or modify infrastructure
mitigations: Require schema validation for all Cursor-generated workflows
Insert a manual approval step before execution
Limit Kestra to dry-run mode for new workflows
Compare generated configs against a known-good template
requires-engineering: add signed artifacts between agents

E_compliance.rationale: Cursor handles source code, open files, and clipboard contents under a closed-source editor model, while Kestra processes logs, inputs, variables, artifacts, and cloud data. The profiles do not state matching residency, retention, or subject-rights controls, so mixed handling of regulated data can create policy mismatch risk; uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed in Cursor open files and then routed into Kestra logs or artifacts
IF the deployment requires residency or retention guarantees not documented in either profile
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of shared workflows
Document retention settings for both tools
Use separate environments for regulated and non-regulated data
Review vendor DPAs before deployment
requires-engineering: implement policy checks on workflow inputs
